# Project Governance 4.3.0

## Improvements

- Approve a bounded local workflow once and reuse it across task revisions and
  successor tasks in the same worktree and host session. Each run still checks
  current task permissions, exact commands, inputs, resources and time limits.
- Context replay refusals now include hashed references that help diagnose changed
  task bindings without exposing prompt or source contents.

## Bug fixes

- Older sibling runtimes can continue their existing workflows in the shared ledger.
  They refuse actions that require the new approval contract.
- Saved run receipts cannot substitute an approval from another workflow.
- Workflow approval can be revoked after source edits or task closure, even when
  the original receipt directory is gone, using its retained grant locator.
- Native checks recognize matching cleanup proof that arrives shortly after exit,
  while preserving failed and unknown execution outcomes.

## Adoption and qualification

This stable minor release follows the normal local source, independent review and
installed archive qualification path. It does not include the separate work-batch
admission candidate. No live provider, physical-device or accepted development cost
claim is made by its controlled tests.

Adoption is deliberate. Existing task-cycle approvals keep their old scope; install
this release and explicitly enroll a workspace workflow to use the new capability.
New approvals expire within 24 hours and remain revocable. Publication does not
upgrade a repository or alter its current runtime pin.
